text: Why is the general quintic equation not solvable by radicals?
choices: Its Galois group S₅ is not a solvable group
Degree-5 polynomials can fail to have roots in ℂ
S₅ contains no element of order 5
explanation: Abel–Ruffini via Galois: a polynomial is solvable by radicals iff its Galois group is solvable, and S₅ is not — its only composition factors are ℤ/2ℤ and the non-abelian simple group A₅. Every complex polynomial of degree 5 still HAS five roots; they just cannot be expressed by radicals in general.
